investigacion.base:
**Bottom line:** As of October 19, 2026, the log lists exactly three withdrawn manuscripts. If nothing changes, this resolves **NO**. There are 10 days left before the deadline.

**What the resolution sources say**
- **history.md** (the latest search copy is about 12 days old) has one dated entry, October 7, 2026. It says a sign error in "Algebraicity of Weil classes on split abelian eightfolds" invalidates a stabilization-trace cancellation argument and the construction used by two dependent papers. The three manuscripts withdrawn are the ones named in the question. The log also says for any withdrawn papers, their README files explain the gap and link to the retracted manuscript. I found no later entry, but my search results may lag behind the live file. Check the file and its commit history directly.
- **Metaculus FAQ:** I didn't pull it up. It only defines what counts as a "credible source," which only matters if history.md goes offline.

**Timeline**
- **Oct 6:** OpenAI posted 722 manuscripts in 372 families of related results. The repository says the model was tested on approximately 4,000 problems.
- **Oct 7:** The first and only log entry: 3 withdrawn, proof repairs in 14 other manuscripts and citation or version updates in 13 additional ones. These are separate revision categories, not further withdrawals. The catalogue dropped to 719. Six new Lean formalizations (machine-checked proofs) brought coverage to 300 of 719 results, about 42%.
- **Oct 8:** Retraction Watch broke the story. An OpenAI spokesperson said roughly half the results were released before formal confirmation.
- **Oct 8–11:** Mathematicians criticised the release, including Tristan Buckmaster and Hugo Duminil-Copin.
- **Oct 15:** A $15M Simons Foundation initiative with OpenAI and Anthropic was announced.
- **Oct 18 (latest coverage):** Articles still describe only the three withdrawals and say the 14 other papers were revised without pulling them from the repository entirely. A table dated Oct 14 marks the withdrawal and revision counts as "May grow".

**Base rates and factors**
- There has been one withdrawal event in about 13 days. All three withdrawals came from a single error that spread to two dependent papers, and nothing new has been withdrawn in the 12 days since.
- OpenAI's habit so far is to repair flawed proofs in place rather than withdraw them (14 repaired vs. 3 withdrawn).
- **Pushing toward YES:** about half the results weren't fully verified at release, about 58% have no Lean proof, outside scrutiny is heavy, and the CM abelian-variety Hodge claim in the same family as the withdrawn papers remains listed and requires its own scrutiny. Related papers can fall together, as the first three did.
- **Pushing toward NO:** the window is short, the repair-in-place habit, and outside review of hard proofs is slow. Some mathematicians reportedly refused to review the release at all.

**Scheduled events:** None that I know of before Oct 29. Further log updates aren't on any announced schedule.

**Prediction markets:** I didn't find any.

criterios: This question resolves YES if, as of 23:59 UTC on October 29, 2026, the history log at https://github.com/openai/math/blob/main/history.md lists more than three (i.e., four or more) distinct manuscripts as withdrawn, counting all withdrawal entries in the log cumulatively since the repository's launch. As of the question's creation the log records exactly three withdrawn manuscripts (announced October 7, 2026: "Algebraicity of Weil classes on split abelian eightfolds", "Algebraicity of Kuga–Satake Correspondences for K3 Surfaces", and "The rational Hodge conjecture for products of K3 surfaces"). The question resolves YES only if at least one additional, distinct manuscript (beyond those three) appears as withdrawn in the log. If history.md is unavailable, resolution will rely on equivalent withdrawal records elsewhere in the repository or on [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions); if no withdrawal information is published anywhere, the question is annulled.
letra_pequena: A manuscript counts as "withdrawn" only if the history log (or an equivalent official repository record) explicitly designates it as withdrawn/retracted. Manuscripts that are merely revised, corrected, updated, or re-titled without being designated as withdrawn do not count. Re-listing or re-describing any of the three already-withdrawn October 7, 2026 manuscripts does not count toward the "more than three" threshold; only distinct additional manuscripts do.
razonamientos:
(a) **Time left:** About 10 days, until 23:59 UTC on October 29, 2026.

(b) **Status quo:** NO. The available record lists exactly three withdrawn manuscripts.

(c) **Reference class:** In this repository’s short history, one error led to a withdrawal event immediately after launch, followed by roughly 12 days with no reported additional withdrawals. That is a thin, launch-skewed base rate, not a reliable daily rate to extrapolate.

(d) **NO scenario:** Scrutiny continues, but any newly identified problems are corrected or remain under review past the deadline.

(e) **YES scenario:** Review uncovers an unfixable flaw in another manuscript, and OpenAI records its withdrawal by the deadline.

(f) **Deciding technicality:** The log must explicitly designate a *distinct fourth manuscript* as withdrawn or retracted. A revision—or another mention of the original three—does not count.

The short remaining window and lack of reported withdrawals since October 7 favor NO, though the number of manuscripts still under scrutiny leaves a meaningful chance of another withdrawal.

Probability: 22%

(a) **Time left:** about 10 days, until 23:59 UTC on October 29, 2026.

(b) **Status quo:** history.md lists exactly three withdrawn manuscripts, all from the single October 7 event. If nothing changes, the question resolves NO.

(c) **Reference class:** post-release corrections of large AI-generated or preprint batches.
- Early errors tend to come in a burst right after release; here that was day 1, with 3 withdrawals and 14 repairs.
- After the burst, the rate drops sharply. There have been about 12 days with no new withdrawals.
- OpenAI repairs far more often than it withdraws (14 repaired versus 3 withdrawn).
- From this, the chance of another withdrawal in a given 10-day window is perhaps 15–25%.

(d) **No scenario:** Scrutiny continues, but deep verification of hard proofs is slow. Any flaws found are patched in place as revisions or errata. history.md gains no new withdrawal entries, or only revision notes, before October 29.

(e) **Yes scenario:** A mathematician or a Lean formalization effort finds an unfixable gap. A plausible target is the CM abelian-variety Hodge claim, or another result in the same family as the withdrawn papers. OpenAI then logs one or more further withdrawals, possibly including dependent papers.

(f) **Technicalities:** Only explicit "withdrawn" or "retracted" designations count, so revisions, corrections and re-titlings do not. My research copy of history.md is about 12 days stale, so an unseen update is possible. However, news coverage as of October 18 still reports only three withdrawals.

Probability: 17%
